title: SLO-aware cost optimizer: safe batching/caching apply + runtime guardrails
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Summary: Implement automated batching/caching configuration recommendations that can be safely applied and rolled back with SLO-aware guardrails. The optimizer will propose per-route batching and caching profiles, execute a staged apply (canary -> ramp -> full), and use runtime limiters, SLO-aware routing, and anomaly detection to prevent regressions in latency or throughput.

Background: We already have telemetry that correlates per-route token distributions, sequence lengths, and latency percentiles. PM has defined a cost-optimization objective that targets 15-30% token-cost reduction per workload while keeping P95 latency and throughput within customer SLOs. Past manual tuning introduced regressions under load spikes; this ticket creates the automation + runtime safety net.

Goals: 
- Automated recommendations engine that suggests batching window, max-batch-size, KV cache TTL and prefix caching eligibility per route.
- Safe apply flow: canary (1% traffic, 5m), ramp (25% 10m), full (100% 30m) with automatic rollback conditions.
- Runtime guardrails: limiters (per-worker concurrent token cap, per-route QPS cap), SLO-aware routing to route traffic to compatible model variants or to Dedicated pool when SLO risks are detected, and anomaly detection that triggers alerts and automated rollback.

Design notes: 
1) Recommendation Engine: uses sampled traces and token histograms to simulate effective batching gains and cache hit uplift. Output is a scored list of candidate configs with estimated cost delta and SLO risk score (low/medium/high).
2) Apply workflow: a feature-flagged controller that performs staged rollout with k-safety checks after each stage. Each stage checks: P50/P95 latency, error rate, throughput, and model token-per-second. If any metric crosses configured thresholds (absolute or relative), rollback to previous config.
3) Limiters: implement per-worker "effective concurrency" limit accounting for batch size and kv-eviction overhead. Implement per-route QPS throttle and per-customer token budget guard to prevent cascading latency from aggressive batching.
4) SLO-aware routing: polling the Console SLO service to decide whether to route new requests to a lower-latency model variant, to Dedicated capacity, or to a cached response path. Routing decisions prioritized by SLO impact score and cost delta.
5) Anomaly detection: rolling-window z-score on P95 and growth-rate detection on queue length. Two tiers of response: soft (notify, tighten limiters) and hard (auto-rollback, switch to fallback model).

Safety considerations and trade-offs: 
- Conservative defaults: only apply recommendations automatically for customer-opted-in workloads or internal test tenants.
- Risk of over-constraining throughput: limiters may reduce peak throughput; we must expose knobs to SREs for emergency override.
- False positives in anomaly detection: tune window sizes and require multi-metric corroboration for auto-rollback.

Acceptance Criteria: see acceptance_criteria field.

Observability and artifacts: dashboards and runbooks will be created. Key dashboards: cost-optimizer/recommendations, runtime/guardrails, slo-health-by-route. Example links: https://console.redwood.internal/dashboards/cost-optimizer (dash), https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4123 (PR).

Rollout plan: internal dogfood -> opt-in beta for 5 customers -> widen to 25% of eligible tenants -> full GA. Each stage gated by absence of SLO violations and manual ops review for first two external customers.
acceptance_criteria: Recommendations engine produces per-route candidate configs with cost delta and SLO risk score for 95% of sampled routes
Controller can perform staged apply with automated checks and rollback triggered within 30s of crossing thresholds
Limiters prevent P95 latency from exceeding SLO by more than 10% in 90% of simulated spike tests
SLO-aware router successfully routes >99% of flagged requests to safe fallback within 500ms of detection in end-to-end tests
Anomaly detector triggers alerts and performs auto-rollback for synthetic injected regressions in staging
comments: 2026-02-25 Ava Chen: Initial RFC written and shared with infra and SRE. Focused on conservative safety defaults and operator overrides.
2026-03-01 Marcus Patel: PoC of the simulator completed; early results show 18% median cost reduction on chat workloads with low risk score for short sequences.
2026-03-04 Design feedback (Sofia Reyes): UX for rollout controls should surface predicted cost vs risk and an undo button. Added to mockups.

2026-03-06 Engineering review: Decided to implement limiters inside the serving runtime rather than as a proxy to reduce added network hops. Trade-off: longer release cycle but lower tail latency impact.
2026-03-09 PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4123 — batching simulator + recommendation CLI. Requesting review from @elaine and @omar-s.

2026-03-11 SRE: Load tests scheduled against staging with spike profile. Early failures showed false positive rollbacks due to noisy P50 variance; mitigation: require correlated P95 and error-rate signal for hard rollback.
2026-03-13 Marcus Patel: Implemented staged canary controller and basic limiter hooks. Next: integrate anomaly detector and SLO service for routing decisions.
